walkthrough:
Multiply through by $\tan^2\theta$ and form a quadratic in $\tan^2\theta$:
$$3\tan^2\theta + 1 = \frac{2}{\tan^2\theta} \implies 3\tan^4\theta + \tan^2\theta - 2 = 0$$

Set the real factor equal to zero (since $\tan^2\theta + 1 > 0$ for all real $\theta$):
$$\tan^2\theta = \frac{2}{3} \implies \tan\theta = \pm\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \approx \pm 0.81650$$

Find all angles within the interval $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\text{From } \tan\theta = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}: \quad \theta_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\right) \approx 39.2^\circ$$
$$\text{From } \tan\theta = -\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}: \quad \theta_2 = 180^\circ - 39.23^\circ \approx 140.8^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 39.2^\circ, \quad 140.8^\circ)$$
